questions.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-5 \\ -3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=7\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & -5 \\ -3 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=12,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $b$ does *not* lie in $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$

questions.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, ${a}_{3}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -9 \\ 13\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10 \\ -16\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -9 \\ 13\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10 \\ -16\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=10 \\ -4{x}_{1}+13{x}_{3}=-16\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 3 & 1 & -9 & 10 \\ -4 & 0 & 13 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -5 \\ -4 & 0 & 13 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=5 \\ {x}_{2}=-5 \\ {x}_{3}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=4.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}-3(4)=5\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=17.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}17{a}_{1}+(-5){a}_{2}+4{a}_{3} & =b \\ 17\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+4\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -9 \\ 13\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10 \\ -16\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=17\cdot (-5)\cdot 4=-340.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$

$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ 3{x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 10 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ {x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}+3(-2)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=8.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}8{a}_{1}+(-2){a}_{2} & =b \\ 8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=8\cdot (-2)=-16.$

questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,4,-5⟩$, $c=⟨3,-9,15⟩$, and  $u=⟨2,-2,11⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ 15\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-s+3t=2 \\ 4s-9t=-2 \\ -5s+15t=11\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 4 & -9 & -2 \\ -5 & 15 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ -5 & 15 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=1,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $s$ and $t$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc=u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $u$ does *not* lie on the plane $Π.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -17\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -17\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -3{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=-17\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 \\ -3 & -5 & -17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}+3(-2)=3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=9.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9{a}_{1}+(-2){a}_{2} & =b \\ 9\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=9\cdot (-2)=-18.$
